headline: Hybrid pangenome alignment and GPU kernels speed up sequence analysis tools
label: Accelerated Genomics Analysis Tools
summary: Recent tools pair GPU parallelization and graph-based references with classical algorithms to cut runtime and reference bias in genomics.
synthesis: The common thread is re-engineering established genomics algorithms for speed, scale, or reference representation. Three items rely on GPU or compiled acceleration: G-ALN ports BWA-aln to GPU with byte-identical output to BWA and about 6-fold faster alignment, ARCHER-LD uses multi-GPU computation for pairwise LD at biobank scale with reported speedups over PLINK, and vardictcpp reimplements VarDictJava in C++17, running about 4-fold faster single-core with up to 17-fold lower memory and identical variant calls. DCSMAP addresses reference bias by routing approximately 14.8% of ML-selected reads from linear alignment to personalized pangenome graphs. Vizitig and Streamline CNV extend this toolkit toward graph-based exploration of colored de Bruijn graphs and a containerized Nextflow workflow for low-pass WGS copy number analysis. What is new is less the individual algorithms than the emphasis on output equivalence with established tools while changing the execution substrate or reference model.
